The test image shows a tomato leaf (appears curled/rolled) with a dense white-gray powdery/fuzzy coating covering most of the leaf surface. The coating is very prominent, covering the leaf uniformly with some darker veins visible through it. Key candidates: **Powdery Mildew**, **Leaf Mold**, **Gray Mold**.

Now I'll view one reference image from each of my top 4 candidates.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Tomato leaf (rolled/curled) showing a very dense, white-gray powdery coating covering the entire leaf surface. The texture is uniform, dusty/powdery, with leaf veins visible through the coating.

- **Powdery Mildew (CDDM_1006)**: Small white scattered patches on green leaf — partial match.
- **Powdery Mildew (CDDM_1061)**: Dense whitish-gray powdery coating covering the full leaf surface — **strong match** to the test image.
- **Leaf Mold (CDDM_1006)**: Olive/grayish fuzzy underside coating — different color/texture than the test image.
- **Gray Mold (Bugwood_15)**: Microscopic view, not comparable at leaf scale.

The dense, uniform white-gray powdery coating across the entire leaf surface is the hallmark of Powdery Mildew. The CDDM_1061 reference is very similar in appearance. Leaf curl can accompany advanced powdery mildew on tomato.
